theme: The Book of Consolation, the New Covenant promise
readingInstruction: Read Jeremiah 30:1-31:40. This is the Book of Consolation, the center of Jeremiah and one of the most important passages in the Old Testament. Read chapter 31 slowly, especially verses 31 to 34. Today’s reading contains the New Covenant.
settingTheScene: After many chapters of judgment, God tells Jeremiah to write in a book all the words he has spoken, and the tone turns to comfort. These chapters were probably written around 587 BC, as Jerusalem was under siege. They promise restoration, a return from exile, and above all, a new covenant. They are the hinge on which the whole unit turns, and the New Testament quotes them more than any other part of Jeremiah.
observation: “Alas! That day is so great there is none like it; it is a time of distress for Jacob; yet he shall be saved out of it” (30:7).
“They shall serve the LORD their God and David their king, whom I will raise up for them” (30:9).
“For I will restore health to you, and your wounds I will heal, declares the LORD” (30:17).
“I have loved you with an everlasting love; therefore I have continued my faithfulness to you” (31:3).
“A voice is heard in Ramah, lamentation and bitter weeping. Rachel is weeping for her children” (31:15).
“Behold, the days are coming, declares the LORD, when I will make a new covenant with the house of Israel and the house of Judah” (31:31).
“I will put my law within them, and I will write it on their hearts. And I will be their God, and they shall be my people” (31:33).
“For I will forgive their iniquity, and I will remember their sin no more” (31:34).
interpretation:
Chapter 30 begins with distress, “a time of trouble for Jacob,” but quickly turns to salvation. God will break the yoke from their neck. They will serve the LORD and a king from David’s line. “For I will restore health to you.” The wound is incurable, but God says he will heal it. The people thought their situation was hopeless. God says that he is the one who made the wound, and he is the one who will heal it.

Chapter 31 opens with a love poem. “I have loved you with an everlasting love.” Before there was a covenant, there was love. “Therefore I have continued my faithfulness to you.” The exile has not ended his love. He promises to build them up again, with joy and dancing. The weeping at Ramah, where the exiles gathered on their way to Babylon, will turn to hope: “There is hope for your future.” Matthew later applies this verse to the weeping of Bethlehem’s mothers.

Then, in verses 31 to 34, the climax. A new covenant. It will not be like the covenant made at Sinai, which the people broke. This time, God himself will write the law on their hearts. The old covenant was written on stone and often kept externally. The new will be internal. There will be four promises: a new heart (“I will write it on their hearts”), a new relationship (“I will be their God, and they shall be my people”), a new knowledge (“they shall all know me, from the least of them to the greatest”), and a new forgiveness (“I will forgive their iniquity, and I will remember their sin no more”).

The closing verses guarantee it. As certain as the sun, moon, and stars, God will not cast off Israel. The new covenant is as secure as creation. It is the heart of the gospel, and it is the memory verse of this unit.
connection: Jesus said at the Last Supper, “This cup that is poured out for you is the new covenant in my blood” (Luke 22:20). Hebrews 8:6-13 and 10:15-18 quote this passage in full, saying that Christ is the mediator of the new covenant. 2 Corinthians 3:3-6 says believers are “a letter from Christ… written not with ink but with the Spirit.” Matthew 2:17-18 quotes Jeremiah 31:15. Romans 11:26-27 speaks of the covenant with Israel.
application:
Take Jeremiah 31:33 with you, and ask what it means that God writes rather than demands.

Take the cup at the Lord’s Supper, and see in it the fulfillment of verse 31.

Ask God to write his law on your heart, so that obedience becomes your desire.
prayerPrompts: Thank God that he has loved you with an everlasting love.
Thank him for the new covenant sealed in Jesus’ blood.
Ask him to write his law on your heart so that obedience becomes your desire.
